note: Published minimal repro from #92399. Bash with run_in_background true and nohup sh -c 'for i in $(seq 1 60); do echo tick $i >> /tmp/bg_probe.log; sleep 1; done' > /dev/null 2>&1 & → completion within ~1s exit 0; immediate ps sometimes empty; wait ~5s and ps lists the process; log keeps growing for 60s after completed.
reproCommand: nohup sh -c 'for i in $(seq 1 60); do echo tick $i >> /tmp/bg_probe.log; sleep 1; done' > /dev/null 2>&1 &
reproSteps: Call the Bash tool with run_in_background: true and the nohup sh -c tick loop command.
Observe: the background task notification arrives within ~1 s and says the command completed with exit code 0.
Immediately call Bash (foreground) with ps aux | grep -v grep | grep 'seq 1 60'. In the observed sessions this sometimes printed nothing.
Wait ~5 s and run the same ps again — the process is listed, and /tmp/bg_probe.log keeps growing for 60 s after the completed notification.
